source: FAO/OIE/World Bank, "Good Practices for Biosecurity in the Pig Sector - Issues and Options in Developing and Transition Countries", FAO Animal Production and Health Paper No. 169, Rome, 2010.
text: When deciding where to build or expand pig housing, keep reasonable distance from other pig farms and from busy roads, since airborne disease spread and vehicle traffic both carry risk over distance; use trees, hedges or a windbreak around the pen area where possible, since these help break up airflow and reduce the distance some airborne pathogens travel; and build a fence sturdy enough to keep out wild or feral pigs (which can carry diseases like classical swine fever and African swine fever) while keeping domestic pigs contained.
